items.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001
items.q: somehow I got hooked up with Pete LaRoca Sims and Dave Liebman and there was — if I could remember the name of the club, they’d know, La Boehme. We worked there six nights a week

ctx.x: You couldn’t have done much better than that.

There was a lot of loft scenes around, and a lot of just sessions. People — I remember working in a club that didn’t pay anything but somehow I got hooked up with Pete LaRoca Sims and Dave Liebman and there was — if I could remember the name of the club, they’d know, La Boehme. We worked there six nights a week and Dave Holland used to come down. There was a lot of us that just — we would play, we would get paid something but not what you would consider very much. There was a lot of playing going on, innovative…

Do you think that, this is a point I was hoping to get to eventually so here we are, do you think that tendency for people to kind of sound like each other is because of the education that’s going on now or what is that about?

items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: George Cables, JoAnne Brackeen, Jimmy Garrison, [Charlie] Haden, Larry Willis. Everybody came through

ctx.x: Not really, unfortunately. That’s the sadness of it all. Brilliant cat, smartest guy probably I’ve ever met, almost too smart. Became a lawyer. It’s more – he’s got a whole story. But anyway, he was – the band was every bass player and every piano player in New York, and me, because I could see, this was it. As soon as I got with him, I could see, this is a heavy guy. I didn’t really know him. I knew he’d been with Trane. I knew the story, etc., etc., but I really didn’t know how he played until he played. It was…
